why: A switch is a device (Component); switching is the forwarding technique (Mechanism).
A bit is a unit of data; bit rate is a property (bits per second); a bit stream is a sequence of bits.
Bandwidth is what a link can carry; throughput is what is measured end to end in practice.
Latency (delay) is one-way; RTT is there and back.

OWNER DECISION NEEDED. Ch. 1 uses bandwidth to mean bits per second (close to data rate); Ch. 2 also uses bandwidth for a range of frequencies in hertz. May be same in one chapter and different in another; a chapter scope may fit better than a book-wide entry.

distinction: protects the receiver vs protects the network
why: Flow control keeps a sender from overrunning the receiver; congestion control keeps senders from overloading the network.
The book uses frame for the link-level data unit and packet for the network-level one (and generically).

distinction: layer and structure of the address
why: A MAC address is a flat link-layer hardware address; an IP address is a hierarchical network-layer address.

distinction: repeats to all ports vs forwards per destination
why: A hub (multiway repeater) sends every frame out of every port; a switch forwards each frame only to the port that leads to its destination.

A switch forwards within one network (link layer); a router forwards between networks (network layer). Owner check: if the book presents a router as a network-layer kind of switch, change kind to kind_of.
Ethernet detects collisions and backs off; 802.11 avoids collisions because a wireless sender cannot detect them.
Detection only finds that a frame is corrupted; correction repairs it from redundant bits.

distinction: level encodes the bit vs transition encodes the bit
why: NRZ maps a bit to a signal level; NRZI marks a 1 with a transition.
Two different block codes with different group sizes; the book calls 8B/10B 'similar', not the same.

distinction: tag within a LAN vs overlay across an IP network
why: A VLAN tags frames to split one LAN; VXLAN carries Ethernet frames inside UDP/IP to build a virtual layer-2 network over layer 3.
Different identifiers for different technologies: a 12-bit VLAN ID in the 802.1Q tag vs a 24-bit VNI in the VXLAN header.
